text:
Marco: Quick heads-up — pushed profiling from last night's canary. Seeing a weird throughput dip when FlashAttention gets picked for small seqs combined with paged-KV churn.
Alex: Interesting, numbers?
Marco: p95 tokens/s down ~18%, p99 latency +120ms on 8k context runs. GPU SM util up slightly but stalls on mem copies.
Priya: Any change in batch sizes or queue compose?
Marco: Yeah that's the odd part — average batch size is stable but batch formation time increases. Looks like the queue is waiting for a preferred kernel match and then paged-KV misses force extra async copies.
Jen: So kernel selection tie-breaker is causing waits? We changed heuristic to prefer FlashAttention for medium sequences last week.
Marco: Exactly. Previously the hybrid kernel would run sooner and avoid the extra KV page fault churn. Now the runtime holds requests hoping for FlashAttention coalescing which rarely happens for this workload.
Alex: Can you paste the hot trace?
Marco: Sure — core of the trace: 
```
[batcher] wait_for_kernel(ms)=12
[kernel_select] prefer=FlashAttention
[paged_kv] miss_count=42
[memcpy_async] queued=42
[kernel_launch] delay_before_launch=45ms
```
Marco: The 45ms delay is killing small-latency buckets.
Priya: Hmm. Two levers: lower queue smoothing window or change kernel preference when paged-KV miss rate > threshold.
Jen: Also consider a token-budget target so batcher stops waiting once token budget goal met for that cycle. Might reduce tail latency.
Alex: Agreed. Can we simulate policy A (smoothing_ms=3) vs policy B (prefer_hybrid_on_kv_miss=true)?
Marco: I ran a quick sim on staging for policy A: p95 regains ~10% but p99 still high. Policy B regains ~14% and reduces memcopy spikes. Combined both gets us close to baseline.
Priya: Nice. Do we have config knobs exposed per-deployment?
Marco: Yes — batcher.queue_smoothing_ms, batcher.token_budget_pct, kernel.selection.kv_miss_threshold. Example change we tested: 
```yaml
batcher:
  queue_smoothing_ms: 3
  token_budget_pct: "0.75"
kernel.selection:
  prefer_flasha_for_medium_seq: false
  kv_miss_threshold: 0.02
```
Alex: Any regressions from throughput perspective? 
Marco: Combined change drops max throughput by ~3% under saturated load, but latency SLOs improve substantially — we think it's worth it for hosted tier and can gate for dedicated customers.
Jen: Sounds like rollout plan: 1) deploy policy B to staging, run 24h perf harness; 2) if stable, roll to canary for low-traffic region; 3) collect perf-bot metrics for 48h.
Priya: I'll own the canary run. Marco, can you add automated detection rule to flip preference when kv_miss > threshold?
Marco: On it. Adding a guard in kernel selector with a metric window.
Alex: Leave a note for runtime QA to repro with mixture of small/medium seqs + paged KV hot churn.
Marco: Added repro script to the bug: `scripts/repro/flasha_pagedkv_churn.sh` and a dataplane flag `--force-hybrid` for testing.
perf-bot: Alert created: runtime/kernel-selector/paged-kv-miss > 0.02 in canary (region us-west-2) — ticket #RDF-3219
Jen: Thanks. Priya — ping me when canary starts and I’ll watch the rollout dashboard. :eyes:
Priya: Will do.
Alex: Good catch Marco. Let's also add a perf regression test to CI that runs the churn scenario weekly.
Marco: Yep, filing that after I push the selector patch.
Jen: OK moving to action items. :thumbsup:
